subject: Is the QCLwR book focused on existing packages or was a new package  developed?

messages.author: 9399a3fae7327c90
messages.subject: Is the QCLwR book focused on existing packages or was a new package  developed?
parts:
Greetings,

I accidentally came across the book on which the group is based while
doing google searches for text mining and linguistics in R. Looking at
the contents page (http://www.routledgelinguistics.com/books/
Quantitative-Corpus-Linguistics-with-R-isbn9780415962704), it seems
like an interesting book and one i would be interested in purchasing
when it is published in the UK (25th Feb '09 i believe).

My question: Is this book based primarily upon existing packages, or
was a new package developed specifically for this book?

My (admittedly limited) use of text mining in R has been using the tm
package, as well as looking at other packages in the R NLP Task View
(http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/NaturalLanguageProcessing.html).

Whether the book has a newly developed package or is focused more upon
existing packages, i think it will be a good study aid and am looking
forward to getting it.

Many thanks,
Tony Breyal

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Is the QCLwR book focused on existing packages  or was a new package developed?
parts:
Hi Tony

Thanks for your interest! For the corpus-linguistic stuff, the book
uses only one package other than the base package, and that is gsubfn.
However, even this package is used only a bit since I wanted to kind
of make a point out of it that only the defaulty functionality coming
with the base package is used. Later in the book I then make one
workhorse function available (exact.matches), which makes several
things much more convenient, though.

Hope that helps,

Cheers,
STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
